claims.text: A predictive approach combining binary-phase-diagram mining with first-principles and Monte Carlo parameters can identify HEA compositions having high lattice disorder and/or multiphase microstructures.
Parameters derived from binary phase diagrams can be used to predict single-solid-solution and composite phase regions in HEAs.
First-principles-parameterized Monte Carlo models can capture intermetallic phase formation and microstructure evolution in Al-containing HEAs.
Phase-diagram variables and first-principles parameters provide compositional markers that correlate with lattice distortion and controlled multiphase structure.
The screening method can select HEA compositions with high lattice distortion and minor multiphase features.
The selected HEAs can be synthesized in single-phase or controlled multiphase states with measurable lattice distortions.
Operating below phase-transformation thresholds and in an inert atmosphere maintains the HEAs' intrinsic lattice disorder.
The relevant structural mediator includes enhanced atomic-scale disorder, lattice distortion, and ultra-nanocrystalline grain structures.
Greater atomic-scale disorder scatters phonons more effectively.
Interfaces between multiple phases scatter phonons more effectively.
Enhanced phonon scattering caused by disorder and phase interfaces lowers phonon thermal conductivity.
HEAs selected by the proposed method will have statistically lower phonon thermal conductivity than HEAs selected by conventional prediction approaches.
The lower phonon thermal conductivity of the selected HEAs will improve thermal-insulation performance.
The proposed method may achieve greater than 80% accuracy in identifying low-thermal-conductivity HEAs.
Conventional thermodynamic or phase-diagram approximations have accuracy around or below 80% for identifying HEAs with low phonon thermal conductivity.
A binary-phase-diagram-based HEA phase classifier has demonstrated overall and single-phase prediction rates above 80%.
The proposed approach is reliable only for HEA systems having available binary phase-diagram data and validated first-principles parameters.
Oxidation or high-temperature phase decomposition may alter intrinsic lattice disorder and limit the method's applicability.
Laser-flash analysis can provide the phonon thermal conductivity used in the proposed benchmark.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant conductivity decrease relative to identically processed conventionally selected controls would falsify the hypothesis.
